title: bwrk global next - ranked cross-project directive queue
description: WHY: this is the PM morning view for humans and the dispatch loop for PM agents - for each project the single most important directive, then one overall. WHAT: bwrk global next [--agent <id>] [--limit <n>] [--json] reads the aggregate rollup cache (never live fan-out - staleness is rendered, not hidden), takes each linked projects top next directives from its rollup, ranks with a deterministic scoring function over severity, subject priority, and aging signals from the sibling task, and returns per-project winners plus the overall winner with the executable command and the project it belongs to (commands rendered with an explicit --workspace <projectRoot> or cd prefix so they run from anywhere). Deterministic tie-breaks by project id then subject id, matching codebase convention. Text mode prints the overall winner command on the last line for shell capture, mirroring bwrk next. Paused, archived, and missing projects are excluded with a note. Fixture tests across three simulated project rollups including one stale and one degraded.
acceptanceCriteria: global next returns per-project and overall winners with executable workspace-qualified commands, deterministic across repeat runs
Stale and degraded projects are surfaced distinctly rather than silently ranked
